title: Vu, lu, reçu, tenu et vécu
summary: Learn high-frequency irregular past participles ending in `u` without inventing a universal rule.
objectives: Retrieve the individual participles of common `-u` verbs.
Use `recevoir` and `tenir` derivatives and distinguish `vécu` from `vu`.

sources.label: Public A2 index: topic-coverage reference only

sections.title: Learn the base verb and its participle together
paragraphs: These participles are irregular: their final `u` is a memory link, not a method for guessing the whole word. `Voir` → `vu` (seen), `devoir` → `dû` (had to), `pouvoir` → `pu` (been able to), `boire` → `bu` (drunk), `croire` → `cru` (believed), `savoir` → `su` (known/found out), `lire` → `lu` (read), `plaire` → `plu` (pleased), `taire` → `tu` (kept quiet about). `Taire` is not the same construction as `se taire`, 'to be silent'.

Use `avoir` in every person: `j'ai lu, tu as lu, il/elle/on a lu, nous avons lu, vous avez lu, ils/elles ont lu`. Replace `lu` with each participle. Keep the circumflex in `dû`, including under the 1990 spelling recommendations. In these examples, no preceding direct object requires agreement.
points: `J'ai pu` often reports a realised opportunity; `je n'ai pas pu` reports inability in a specific situation. `J'ai su` can mean 'I found out'. Context decides the English translation.
`Plaire` reverses the English 'like' perspective: `ce film m'a plu` means I liked this film; the film is the subject.

examples.french: J'**ai vu** l'annonce et j'**ai lu** les conditions.
examples.english: I saw the advertisement and read the conditions.

examples.french: Nous **avons dû** attendre, mais nous **avons pu** entrer.
examples.english: We had to wait, but we were able to enter.

examples.french: Elle **a bu** de l'eau et **a cru** mon explication.
examples.english: She drank water and believed my explanation.

examples.french: J'**ai su** la vérité ; il **a tu** un détail.
examples.english: I found out the truth; he kept one detail quiet.

mistakes.why: The auxiliary needs a past participle, not `devoir`.

sections.title: Longer `-u` families
paragraphs: `Recevoir` → `reçu`; `apercevoir` → `aperçu`; `concevoir` → `conçu`; `décevoir` → `déçu`; `percevoir` → `perçu`. The cedilla keeps the soft `c` sound before `u`. `Tenir` → `tenu`, with `retenir` → `retenu`, `obtenir` → `obtenu`, `maintenir` → `maintenu` and `soutenir` → `soutenu`. `Vivre` → `vécu`; `survivre` → `survécu`. These are all `avoir` verbs in the constructions here, unlike `venir` → `venu` with `être`.
points: All persons: `j'ai reçu, tu as reçu, il/elle/on a reçu, nous avons reçu, vous avez reçu, ils/elles ont reçu`. Substitute `tenu`, `obtenu`, `vécu` and the other family members.

examples.french: Elle **a obtenu** un permis et **a tenu** sa promesse.
examples.english: She obtained a permit and kept her promise.

practice.prompt: Give only the participle of voir: Nous avons ___ le médecin.
Give only the participle of devoir: Elle a ___ annuler.
Passé composé of recevoir: Tu ___ un rappel.
Passé composé of tenir: Nous ___ la porte.
Give the participle of pouvoir: Ils ont ___ payer.
Give the participle of boire: Vous avez ___ du thé.
Give the participle of croire: J'ai ___ cette histoire.
Give the participle of savoir: Tu as ___ la nouvelle hier.
practice.explanation: Savoir becomes su, here found out.

production_task.prompt: Describe an application you completed: the information you read, a requirement, something you received and the result.
production_task.model_answer: J'ai lu les conditions. J'ai dû fournir une photo, mais j'ai pu envoyer le dossier en ligne. J'ai reçu une confirmation et j'ai obtenu mon permis.
production_task.translation: I read the conditions. I had to provide a photo, but I was able to send the application online. I received a confirmation and obtained my permit.
rubric: State a clear outcome without assuming `voulu` or `pu` always guarantees every result.
